chunks.text:
Hi Nicky,

It was yesterday. You sent me the video of you practicing piano. "Welcome to Seb's," from La La Land. The song that plays when he finally opens his club, when the dream becomes real. Seeing you at the keys, after our recent chat at Old York on agency, makes me so happy. The happiness doesn't need explanation, but I'll try anyway: you chose to become, and I get to witness.

You know how the film ends. Mia walks into Seb's club, five years later, with her husband. They see each other across the room. The montage plays: the life they might have had, the kiss on the bench, the house with the view. And then it dissolves back to what is. They share a look. A small smile. An acknowledgment: _we happened, and we're okay, and this is what we became instead._ Just the quiet recognition that some loves don't fit the shape you wanted, and that's not a failure. Seb plays the song. Mia leaves. The credits roll.

I think about that ending a lot. I've moved on. Not from you, but from the shape I thought we should take. The romantic possibility closed. What remained was something I still don't have a name for. Platonic, but that word is too thin. Love, but that word gets read wrong. Something that exists in the vocabulary we built together, that doesn't translate outside it.

This year held Topanga, and everything after. I wrote you a [piece](/posts/her) in January that metamorphosed from gratitude into something I hadn't planned to say. You responded kindly, clearly: friendship was what we had and what we should keep. The months after were [processing](/posts/a-broken-heart): confusion about where friendship ends and love begins, the slow work of staying in something after the romantic possibility closed. I wrote too much about it. I wrote you [a philosophical essay](/posts/25/n-bday) in November. You didn't read it, which is fine. It was as much for me as for you.

But there's one idea from it I want you to have:

```quotes
Choosing friendship after romantic rejection wasn't settling for less. It was recognizing that what we'd built (the interpretive project, the shared semantic space, the ongoing work of learning each other) didn't need romance to justify it. It justified itself.

aarnphm
```

We return to each other again and again, but each return happens from a slightly different position, with a slightly revised understanding. This is the infrastructure of [love](/thoughts/love): choosing to remain in interpretation rather than settling for a fixed image.

I kept trying to resolve us into one category or another: "just friends," "over it," "moved on." The resolution never came because it was the wrong question. The romantic/platonic binary is too coarse.

Ava writes about how friendship uses romantic circuitry, how close friendships are inherently romantic because they're inherently intimate.[^ava] Romantic relationships come with certain scripts: exclusivity, cohabitation trajectories, future-projection. Friendship has no template. It constructs itself, finds its own shape. What we have constructs itself.

---

You can't make someone become. You can only create conditions. If my care made you more predictable, more dependent, more reduced to what I wanted you to be, it would have failed by its own logic. The piano video is evidence of success by a different metric: you surprised me. You're still surprising me. The interpretation stays alive because you keep becoming someone I need to learn again.

That dinner two weeks ago at Old York. The corner booth where we'd sit across from each other, trading ideas. You listen with your whole body. I notice: the way you tilt your head when something lands, the small nod before you push back, the attentive silence that means you're actually considering what I said rather than waiting to respond. Our ideological differences became the whole point of our game. The sparring itself was the intimacy.

We didn't have our birthday dinner this year. Life got busy, you said. I understood what you meant. You needed distance. The feelings were still too close, too recent. The necklace came back, too. Not because you didn't want it. You were clear about that. Because of principle. Something about not accepting gifts you couldn't reciprocate in kind. I respect that more than I can say. You were teaching me, again, who you actually are.

I spent the year in a ::liminal stage::. Not being ready for living yet, still doing. If summer is for summoning what you desire, then winter is for becoming what you endure. December arrived without permission. The sun stands still for tender, perilous questions.

Kafka wrote to Milena about how written kisses don't reach their destination. They're drunk on the way by ghosts.[^kafka] A confession meant as appreciation transforms, by the act of sending, into something that can't be taken back. The letter drifts into the void and you watch three bubbles appear and disappear. The ghosts got most of my January letter. What remained was just enough truth to reorganize everything.

I've been processing by writing. Henrik calls it dialogue with past versions of yourself.[^henrik] Interviewing myself, drilling down: _what do you mean by that? what do you actually want? what are you confused about?_ The confusion surfaces specific things. The specific things become vocabulary. The vocabulary doesn't resolve the feeling but it lets me hold it differently.

We're not the people we were in January. The versions of us who went through Topanga, who chose to keep building after, who arrived at this December. The relationship holds all of them. It's denser now.

---

```quotes
There are nights I become the envelope and you are the letter; the world is only a stamp.

aarnphm
```

That's from the poem I wrote for your birthday. A week later came the [manual for the wounds](/posts/a-manual-for-the-wounds): sitting with the splinter until it names itself. The wound is still breathing. But it's less raw now.

What I want you to know: the confusion isn't suffering. We didn't choose to meet. We didn't choose for the friendship to develop this particular shape. I didn't choose to feel what I felt in January. I did choose what to do with it. The choosing continues.

You wanted me to keep learning you. That's what you were testing, three years ago, when you said you wanted me to see you as you really are. I'm still learning. Memory replays old moments, Sherry says, not to torture us but to see if we can bear to look again, and if the looking might change us.[^sherry] The looking changed me. I can bear to look now.

---

Thank you for the video. Thank you for choosing to practice again. Thank you for remaining in the interpretation with me, even when remaining got complicated, even after you knew how I felt.

I love you in a way that defies categorization. It's the kind of love that would cross continents for a single afternoon together. That remembers your nut allergy with the same vigilance I remember to breathe. That wants to send you nice perfumes that I come across.

It continues. Happy holidays, signing out.

[^sign]

[^kafka]: franz kafka, _letters to milena_ (letter of march 1922): "written kisses don't reach their destination, rather they are drunk on the way by the ghosts."

[^henrik]: henrik karlsson, "writing in a way that gets your thoughts to flow." rewriting is dialogue with past versions of yourself. the interesting ideas emerge from letting multiple selves layer comments on the same topic.

[^sherry]: sherry ning, "my year of ecstasy and insecurities" (2025). memory replays old moments not to torture us but to see if we can bear to look again, and if the looking might change us.

[^ava]: ava, "is friendship romantic?" from the friendship series on bookbear express. close friendships use romantic circuitry, just with different structure: the substance is the same, the scripts are different.
